title: Quercetin improves cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by promoting microglia/macrophages M2 polarization via regulating PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Li, Lin; Jiang, Weifeng; Yu, Baojian; Liang, Huiqi; Mao, Shihui; Hu, Xiaowei; Feng, Yan; Xu, Jiadong; Chu, Lisheng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究槲皮素通过PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB通路促进小胶质细胞M2极化改善脑缺血再灌注损伤，属纯细胞/动物实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The modulation of microglial polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype shows promise as a therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke. Quercetin, a natural flavonoid abundant in various plants, possesses anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and antioxidant properties. Nevertheless, its effect and underlying mechanism on microglia/macrophages M1/M2 polarization in the treatment of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CI/RI) remain poorly explored. In the current study, we observed that quercetin ameliorated neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume, decreased the number of M1 microglia/macrophages (CD16/32(+)/Iba1(+)), and enhanced the number of M2 microglia/macrophages (CD206(+)/Iba1(+)) after establishing the CI/RI model in rats. Subsequent in vivo and in vitro experiments indicated that quercetin downregulated M1 markers (CD86, iNOS, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6) and upregulated M2 markers (CD206, Arg-1, IL-10, and TGF-beta). Network pharmacology analysis and molecular docking revealed that the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway emerged as the core pathway. Western blot confirmed that quercetin upregulated the phosphorylation of PI3K and Akt, while alleviating the phosphorylation of IkappaBalpha and NF-kappaB both in vivo and in vitro. However, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 reversed the effects of quercetin on M2 polarization and the expression of key proteins in the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB pathway in primary microglia after oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) in vitro. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that quercetin facilitates microglia/macrophages M2 polarization by modulating the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway in the treatment of CI/RI. These findings provide novel insights into the therapeutic mechanisms of quercetin in ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 调节小胶质细胞从促炎M1表型向抗炎M2表型的极化，作为缺血性卒中的治疗策略显示出前景。槲皮素（quercetin）是一种在多种植物中丰富的天然黄酮类化合物，具有抗炎、抗凋亡和抗氧化特性。然而，其在脑缺血/再灌注损伤（CI/RI）治疗中对小胶质细胞/巨噬细胞M1/M2极化的作用及潜在机制仍鲜有探讨。在本研究中，我们观察到，在建立大鼠CI/RI模型后，槲皮素改善了神经功能缺损，减少了梗死体积，降低了M1型小胶质细胞/巨噬细胞（CD16/32(+)/Iba1(+)）的数量，并增加了M2型小胶质细胞/巨噬细胞（CD206(+)/Iba1(+)）的数量。随后的体内和体外实验表明，槲皮素下调了M1标志物（CD86、iNOS、TNF-alpha、IL-1beta和IL-6），并上调了M2标志物（CD206、Arg-1、IL-10和TGF-beta）。网络药理学分析和分子对接揭示，PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路为核心通路。Western blot证实，槲皮素在体内和体外均上调了PI3K和Akt的磷酸化，同时减轻了IkappaBalpha和NF-kappaB的磷酸化。然而，在体外氧糖剥夺/再复氧（OGD/R）后的原代小胶质细胞中，PI3K抑制剂LY294002逆转了槲皮素对M2极化及PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB通路关键蛋白表达的影响。总体而言，我们的研究结果表明，槲皮素通过调节PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路，在CI/RI治疗中促进小胶质细胞/巨噬细胞M2极化。这些发现为槲皮素在缺血性卒中中的治疗机制提供了新的见解。
